summary: Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1948 to 1953. He later held a post at Hokkaido University from circa 1957 to 1968.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Japanology, Hiroshi Kanaseki studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1952. He later held a post at Tenri University from circa 1982 to 1998.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Hiroshi Kanno studied at the University of Tokyo. He directed the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2009) and became a professor at the International University of Health and Welfare in 2015.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Hiroshi Kuroda studied at Kyoto University until 1976. He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1990) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (attested 1988).

Hiroshi Marui, an Indologist and philosopher, studied at the University of Tokyo, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Toho Kenkyukai, Musashino University, and served as assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (1999–2018).
Working in Indology and other fields, Hiroshi Maruyama was attested as a professor at Osaka University and head of the Ayurveda Research Society in 1987.
Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Hiroshi Nemoto completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he was later attested as a professor between 2015 and 2026.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Hiroshi Tokushige held posts at Koyasan University, where he was attested as a commissioned researcher in 2015 and as a specially appointed lecturer in 2026.

Active in Indology and religious studies, Hiroshi Yamashita studied as an international student at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University, attested from 1996 to 1999.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Hirotaka Kato was attested as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism in 2015 and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University, attested from 2010 to 2012.
Active in philosophy and other fields, Hiroyuki Kato held positions at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), the Kaisei School (~1862–1869), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929. He later held an academic post at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1969 to 1983.

Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kobe University, Ryukoku University, and the University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and other fields, Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University. He served as a professor at Kobe University (~1970–1982) and Komazawa University (~1982–1989), and was named professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1982).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Hisao Takahashi studied at Taisho University and under Ryukai Mano. He held several posts at Taisho University, serving as professor from circa 1996 to 2015.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Hisashi Matsumura studied under Jan Willem de Jong. He held positions at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and Kobe Shinwa University as an assistant professor (attested 1996).

A scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology, Hisashi Sato studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1963–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and taught at Bukkyo University (~1977–1987).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Hisataka Ishida studied at the University of Tokyo and under Helmut Krasser at the University of Vienna. He was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

Hisatake Kato was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held posts at Yamagata University, Tohoku University, the University of Tokyo (~1989–1998), Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and the University of Human Arts and Sciences.
